Allow.description:
What a replacement may change besides adding declarations: the values of
the named definitions.

definitions.description:
The definitions whose value may change, e.g. to add a missing
hypothesis; their types and theorems' types stay the same. A theorem's
type only names a definition, so its meaning can change: the response
lists the theorems that use a changed definition. Each is a definition
of the replaced snapshot's module or of a snapshot the code no longer
builds on, else the create's `check.error` is a `bad_request` and
nothing is kept. Names are compared with a private one's module left
out, so a `private def h` is `_private.h`, or its full name as a
refusal gives it, but not `h`, as the error for `h` says. An empty
list is a `bad_request`: to change none, leave `allow` out.

ApplyTacticRequest.description: `POST /states/{id}/tactic`. A failing tactic is a 422 with kind `lean`.

complete.description:
No goals remain for this state's `sorry`. This says nothing about the
rest of the proof; check the assembled proof with the session check.

state.description: The new state. Earlier states stay valid, so a session is a tree.

AtPosition.description:
What Lean recorded at a position asked about in `at`. Each part is
absent when no syntax of its kind written in the code contains the
position; the innermost one is reported, the range that starts last,
then ends first.

tactic.description: The tactic at the position, with the goals before and after it.

term.description:
With `detail: ["terms"]`, the term at the position that Lean
elaborated against an expected type. Lean gives the head of an
application the application's: on `f` in `f x`, this is `f`,
expecting what `f x` was expected to be.

in_spec.description:
With `against`: whether the spec permits it, as declared in a spec
snapshot's module or in a module that one builds on. Names are
compared with a private one's module left out.

signature.description: As written, from its module's declaration export.

snapshot_id.description:
A snapshot of the module that declares it: one with the labels, or
a head, if there is one.

used_by.description: The snapshots' declarations that rest on it.

verified.description: Its module has passed the kernel re-check.

AuditFork.description: A snapshot that more than one snapshot replaces.

replaced_by.description: The snapshots that replace it, oldest first.

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot replaced more than once.

AuditLink.description:
A link that let definitions change: `snapshot_id` replaces another
snapshot with an `allow`, and its create's comparison found what changed.

replacement.description:
What its create's comparison with the replaced snapshot found, as
[`CreateSnapshotResponse::replacement`] gave it.

replaces.description:
Its link, as its [`Snapshot::replaces`] shows it: the replaced
snapshot, which may have been deleted since, and the `allow`.

AuditSnapshotsResponse.description:
`GET /snapshots/audit`: what the snapshots that have every label the
query names (as in a listing) rest on. Statuses come from the build's
axiom report, or the kernel re-check once a module is verified, so a
trusted audit has no `rejected` or `sorry` and `unverified_modules` 0.
Whether an assumption is reasonable is for review.

With `against=<snapshot id>` instead of labels, repeatable, it audits a
run against its spec, the snapshots named. From each, it follows the
snapshots that [`replace`](CreateSnapshotRequest::replaces) it, whatever
their labels, to the run's `heads`, and judges each spec declaration on
each head it reaches. The counts are then those of the heads' snapshots.
The ids are of one version, which the audit uses, and `label` doesn't
combine with them. A spec snapshot that doesn't exist is `not_found`.

assumptions.description:
The assumptions what the snapshots declare uses, by name, wherever
they are declared.

clean.description:
With `against`: whether the run is done. There is no fork, and every
target is accepted on its head: the head's module is verified, and
the target is `proved`, or `conditional` on assumptions the spec
permits (see [`AuditAssumption::in_spec`]).

forks.description:
With `against`: the snapshots on the run that more than one snapshot
replaces. The run isn't clean until all but one branch are deleted.

heads.description:
With `against`: the snapshots the run ends at, which nothing
replaces, each once, in the order the walk reached them. A snapshot
replaced by one that was deleted since is a head again, as the
deleted snapshot held the link.

links.description:
With `against`: the links that allowed definitions to change, for
review: those on the way from the spec snapshots to the heads, and
those of the spec snapshots' own chains back through what they
replaced, as far as those snapshots exist.

targets.description:
With `against`: each declaration of a spec snapshot's module, other
than its assumptions and what Lean generated, on each head reached
from that spec snapshot. A replacement keeps every declaration of what
it replaces, so every head carries them all.

AuditSummary.description:
The snapshots' declarations by status, each module's once, without the
assumptions themselves and what Lean generated.

unverified_modules.description:
The snapshots' modules that haven't passed the kernel re-check, so
whose statuses come from the build's report.

AuditTarget.description: A spec declaration, as a head of the run declares it.

head.description: The head, reached from `spec`, whose declaration this is.

name.description:
Its name as the spec snapshot's module declares it, so a private
one's names the spec's module. The head's declaration is the one
with the same name, a private one's module left out.

spec.description: The spec snapshot that declares it.

verified.description: The head's module has passed the kernel re-check.

axioms.description: Its axioms outside the allowed list.

snapshot_id.description: A snapshot with the labels, or a head, whose module declares it.

items.description: The code to check; each item gets a result, in this order.

at.description: Up to 64 positions in the code to report on: [`CheckResult::at`].

version.description: Worker pool label or alias; defaults to the server's default.

at.description: With `at`, what Lean recorded at each position, in request order.

declarations.description: Declarations the code added, with the axioms each depends on.

error.description: Why the check could not complete (timeout, crash, policy, ...).

messages.description: Lean's messages, with positions in the submitted code.

ok.description:
True when the code elaborated without errors and passed every policy
check: only standard axioms, no metaprogramming, allowed options, and
for session checks, the session's original statements.

reasons.description: Why `ok` is false, e.g. "axiom: t uses sorryAx".

tactics.description:
With `detail: ["tactics"]`, one entry each time a tactic in the code
ran, in the order Lean ran them. A tactic run on several goals, as
under `all_goals` or `<;>`, appears once per run, and so does every
alternative `first` tried.

time.description: Seconds Lean spent on the code.

CheckSessionRequest.description:
`POST /sessions/{id}/check`: re-checks completed code from scratch
and confirms it proves the statements the session started from, with the
same imports.

CreateSnapshotRequest.description:
`POST /snapshots`: checks code like `/check` and, if Lean accepts it,
keeps it as a module that later code can import, with a new snapshot of
it. Code that is already kept gets a new snapshot of its module without
being built again.

key.description:
Makes the create safe to retry: while a snapshot made with this key
exists, a create with it on the same code returns that snapshot as it
is, instead of adding another; on other code it is a `bad_request`.
Such a replay ignores the request's other fields, `labels` and
`verify` included, so it can be `verified: false` with no error after
`verify: true`. Creates that keep nothing don't use the key up, and
deleting the snapshot frees it. See
[`check_key`](crate::labels::check_key) for the rules.

labels.description:
The new snapshot's labels; see
[`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels) for the rules.

replaces.description:
The snapshot this code replaces, e.g. the skeleton a proof fills in.
The code is kept only if it still declares everything that snapshot's
module declares, each the same kind of declaration with the same type
and, for definitions, the same value unless `allow` names them, and
adds no assumptions (`axiom`s, its own or a newly imported
snapshot's); it may add other declarations and imports. If it no
longer builds on a snapshot that module does, what the module's
declarations use from there must be unchanged in what the code builds
on now. Otherwise nothing is kept and `check.reasons` lists the
changes. The new snapshot records the link.

timeout.description:
Lean's time limit in seconds, for building the module including its
imports.

verify.description:
Whether to re-check the code through the kernel. `true` also re-checks
its imports, so the snapshot ends [`verified`](Snapshot::verified) or
the check has an error, except on a [`key`](Self::key) replay. `false`
never re-checks. By default, only code that uses macros, its own or an
import's, is re-checked.

version.description:
Worker pool label or alias. By default, the version of the snapshot
`replaces` names, if any, else the server's default. A version other
than that snapshot's is a `bad_request`.

check.description:
The check, as for `/check`. It has no `sorries`, and `time` includes
importing the module's imports.

replacement.description:
What the replacement changed, if the request named a snapshot it
replaces and the code was kept. Absent on a key replay, which doesn't
compare again.

snapshot.description:
The snapshot this create added, or on a
[`key`](CreateSnapshotRequest::key) replay the one the key is on.
Absent when nothing new was kept: Lean reported errors, the check
could not complete, the code changed what the snapshot it
[`replaces`](CreateSnapshotRequest::replaces) states (`check.reasons`
says how), or `verify: true` found it kept but failing the re-check
(`check.error` says why).

Declaration.description: A new declaration and the axioms it depends on.

assumes.description:
Its axioms that are assumptions: declared as `axiom` in this code or
in a snapshot it builds on.

generated.description:
Made by Lean on demand, such as an equation lemma: code with the same
statements needn't have it.

status.description: What its axioms make it, by [`ProofStatus`].

type_hash.description:
A hash of its type, with private names taken without their module,
and with the internal auxiliaries it uses folded in.

type_refs.description:
The constants of this code and of the snapshots it builds on that its
type uses, through internal auxiliaries.

value_hash.description:
For definitions, a hash of the value, as of the type, so a proof can't
change what a statement means by redefining something it mentions.

value_refs.description:
The same for a definition's value, or an inductive's constructors and
recursor.

dependencies.description: Declarations it uses, in its statement and its proof or body.

description.description: What it states, in words, when a description exists.

type_full.description: The type with full names and no notation.

used_by.description: Declarations that use it, most prominent first (at most 50).

DeleteSnapshotResponse.description:
`DELETE /snapshots/{id}`: deletes the snapshot. Its module goes too once
no snapshot and no kept module needs it, and then so do the modules it
imports, on the same terms.

removed.description: The modules removed, the snapshot's own first.

Description.description: A natural-language description of a declaration.

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. "lsv2-v4.28.0-rc1" or a model name.

title.description:
What the declaration is called in words, e.g. "Subadditivity of von
Neumann entropy".

Detail.description: Extra detail a check can return, requested in `detail`.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

Export.description:
A declaration of a snapshot's module, as code that imports it sees it,
with its description once search has written one (with
`PISA_SEARCH_DESCRIBE_MODEL`).

additive_sibling.description: The `to_additive` counterpart, folded into this hit.

imports.description:
The import header that loads it, when the index's default header
(`import Mathlib` and `import Physlib`) doesn't.

informal.description: A Physlib informal result: stated, not proved.

uses_sorry.description: Depends on `sorry`: not usable as a proof step.

version.description: The version the index was built from.

Health.description: `GET /health`: 200, or 503 once the server is stopping.

oneOf.description: Search's state; `null` if the server doesn't search.

status.description: `draining`, with a 503, once the server is stopping.

workers.description: The live workers on the queue; `null` if it can't be read.

score.description: Fused score; only comparable within one query.

snapshot_ids.description:
For a declaration of a snapshot module (named in `module`, with the
header that loads it in `flags.imports`): the ids of the query's
snapshots of the module, newest first, at most 10.

status.description:
For a snapshot module's declaration: what its own axioms make it, as
in the snapshot API, so a proved lemma next to a `sorry` is `proved`.

summary.description: One or two sentences describing it, when a description exists.

text.description: About 150 tokens for a model's context.

title.description:
What it is called in words, when a description exists, e.g.
"Subadditivity of von Neumann entropy".

verified.description:
For a snapshot module's declaration: its module and everything the
module imports passed the kernel re-check.

Job.description: An async request, as `/jobs/{id}` reports it until it is done.

id.description:
Its id: 32 hex digits, to keep secret, as anyone who has it can read
the answer or cancel the job.

JobKind.description: The endpoint an async request ran.

JobOutcome.description:
What `GET /jobs/{id}` answers once the job is done: what its request
would have. By `kind`: `check` and `check_session` a `CheckResult`,
`start_session` a `Session`, `apply_tactic` an `ApplyTacticResponse`,
`create_snapshot` a `CreateSnapshotResponse`, `verify_snapshot` a
`VerifySnapshotResponse` and `rebuild_snapshots` a
`RebuildSnapshotsResponse`. An error is the request's own, with its
status.

ListDependentsResponse.description:
`GET /snapshots/{id}/dependents`: the snapshots of every module that
imports the snapshot's module, directly or through others, parents first:
by level, where a module that imports it is at level 1 and one that
imports that at 2, by its longest chain, then oldest first. With
`label=key:value` filters, as in a listing, only the snapshots with every
label.

ListSnapshotsResponse.description:
`GET /snapshots`: the version's snapshots, newest first, that have every
label the query names as `label=key:value` (split on the first `:`; up to
64 filters), at most `limit` of them (1 to 1000, default 100). Keep
requesting with `next` as `after` while a page has it.

next.description:
Where the next page starts, if this page is full. The page after it
may be empty.

Pos.description:
A position in the submitted code: lines count from 1, and columns from 0
in Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units.

ProofStatus.description:
What a declaration's axioms make it, besides the allowed ones (by default
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`), worst last.

Query.description:
One search. Fill as many fields as you can: each feeds different lanes,
and more fields mean better fusion.

goal.description: A pretty-printed goal state (hypotheses and `⊢ target`).

include_sorried.description: Also return declarations that depend on `sorry`, flagged.

latex.description: The statement in LaTeX, e.g. `S(\rho_{AB}) \le S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B)`.

name.description: A declaration name, possibly partial or misspelled.

pattern.description: A Lean expression or pattern, e.g. `Matrix.trace ?A = 1`.

snapshots.description: Snapshots to search as well as the base libraries (default: none).

text.description: Free text from a person; classified as natural language, LaTeX, Lean or a name.

dense_pending.description:
The dense lane was left out because the query is still being
embedded; asking again shortly will likely include it.

warnings.description: What made this result worse than usual, e.g. a lane that failed.

new_snapshot_id.description: The snapshot the create made, or replayed.

check.description:
The create's check: Lean's errors, a refused replacement's
`reasons`, or the `error` that stopped it.

RebuildItem.description:
A create in a [`RebuildSnapshotsResponse`]: `POST /snapshots` with its
`code`, `labels`, `key` and `replaces`.

affected.description:
The theorems of the module whose type uses a changed definition,
directly or through other definitions, here or below.

code.description: The old module's code with its imports swapped.

key.description:
The idempotency key to create it with. Planning again gives the same
keys, so running a plan again after a failure replays the creates
that are done.

level.description:
The wave its create runs in: one more than the highest level among
the items whose modules it imports and the item it replaces, so 1 for
one that imports only `from`'s module and replaces no item.

new_header.description: The header of code on top of the new module.

replaces.description:
What the new snapshot replaces, to send as the create's `replaces`,
the links mirroring the old ones. If the snapshot it rebuilds
replaced one the plan also rebuilds, it replaces that one's new
snapshot, `item`, with its own link's `allow`: a skeleton's proof
replaces the rebuilt skeleton, and is compared with it. If it
replaced one the plan doesn't rebuild, it replaces that same
snapshot, with its own link's `allow` and, when `to` replaces `from`
and that snapshot builds on `from`, `to`'s: a proof whose skeleton
doesn't build on `from` still replaces the skeleton. Otherwise, when
`to` replaces `from`, it replaces the snapshot it rebuilds, with
`to`'s `allow`. The create then checks that nothing its statements
depend on changed, and is refused if something did.

snapshot_id.description:
The snapshot it rebuilds. Absent for a module that only links others
to `from`, with no snapshot that has the labels: it gets the labels
asked for.

RebuildLink.description:
What a rebuilt snapshot replaces: a snapshot that exists, `snapshot_id`,
or the new snapshot of another item of the plan, `item`. Exactly one is
set. A create sends it as [`Replaces`], with `item` mapped to the
`new_snapshot_id` created for that item.

item.description:
The index in `plan` of the item whose new snapshot it replaces. That
item is at a lower level.

snapshot_id.description:
The replaced snapshot: the one the item rebuilds, or the one that
snapshot replaced if the plan doesn't rebuild it.

RebuildSkipped.description:
A [`RebuildItem`] not created, because it builds on, or replaces, one
that wasn't.

RebuildSnapshotsRequest.description:
`POST /snapshots/rebuild`: plans how to create the dependents of `from`
(see [`ListDependentsResponse`]) again on `to`, each with its imports of
`from`'s module, and of the other modules it rebuilds, swapped for the new
ones, and unless `dry_run` creates them: a level at a time, a level's
creates side by side once the level below is done. `from` and `to` are of
one version, which the rebuild runs on.

allow_changes.description:
Plan even though `to` changes what `from` states, when `to` wasn't
created to [`replace`](CreateSnapshotRequest::replaces) `from`.

dry_run.description: Only plan: the client creates the plan's items.

labels.description:
Which dependents to rebuild: those with a snapshot that has every
label, and the modules they build on above `from`. Required, so that
the caller chooses which projects follow the edit.

retire.description:
Once every item is created, delete the old snapshots the plan rebuilt,
from the top down, and with them the old modules nothing else needs.
`from` stays: delete it yourself if nothing needs it.

RebuildSnapshotsResponse.description:
What a rebuild planned and, unless it was a dry run, did. Sending the same
rebuild again plans the same items with the same keys, so the creates that
are done replay their snapshots, and the rest run.

changed_definitions.description:
The definitions whose value `to` changed: when `to` replaces `from`,
among those its `allow` names.

changes.description:
How `to` differs from `from`, as in a refused replacement's
`check.reasons`. Empty when `to` replaces `from`: its create compared
them.

created.description: For a run, the items created, in plan order.

failed.description: For a run, the items whose create kept nothing.

ok.description:
For a plan, whether there is one: false when `to` changes what `from`
states and `allow_changes` isn't set. For a run, whether every item
was created, and retired if asked.

plan.description:
The creates to make, by level, then oldest first. A level's items can
be created together once the level below is done.

retired.description: With `retire`, the ids of the old snapshots deleted, top down.

skipped.description:
For a run, the items not created because they build on, or replace,
one that failed or was skipped. Other branches go on.

Replacement.description:
What a replacement changed, as the create's comparison with the snapshot
it [`replaces`](CreateSnapshotRequest::replaces) found.

affected.description:
The theorems whose type uses a changed definition, directly or
through another definition.

changed_definitions.description:
The definitions whose value changed, each of them one that `allow`
names.

filled.description:
The replaced module's declarations that used `sorry` and no longer
do.

Replaces.description:
A snapshot that a create replaces, and what the replacement may change:
a create's [`replaces`](CreateSnapshotRequest::replaces), and the link the
new snapshot keeps.

allow.description:
The definitions the replacement may change besides adding
declarations; by default none.

snapshot_id.description:
The replaced snapshot. A create's is of the create's version, and
chooses it when the create names none, ahead of the server's default.

deprecated_to.description: For a deprecated name, its replacement.

suggestions.description: Closest existing names, best first; empty for an exact match.

version.description:
A version, or an alias of one: the index's, or its snapshots'. Any
other fails with `not_found`.
The version the index was built from.

error.description: Why the index isn't open yet.

leader.description: This replica leads the snapshot index.

ready.description: The index is open and Qdrant answers, so searches can be served.

version.description: The version the index was built from.

A version, or an alias of one: the index's, or its snapshots'. Any
other fails with `not_found`.
The version the index was built from.

Session.description: A proof session: the states that its code's `sorry`s start from.

id.description: Its id, for checking the finished proof at `/sessions/{id}/check`.

Snapshot.description:
Kept code: a module that later code imports, with labels. Every snapshot
of the same code shares one module, which stays while a snapshot of it, or
a kept module that imports it, needs it.

created.description: When it was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

header.description:
The header to start code on top of this snapshot with: its code's
imports with its snapshots replaced by this one. Code with exactly
this header reuses the Lean process the snapshot's builder keeps warm.

id.description:
Its id, `<version>~<32 lowercase hex>`, which the other snapshot
endpoints take. It carries the version, so they need no other.

module.description:
The module to import, e.g. `PisaSnap.s1a2b…`, shared by every snapshot
of the same code.

replaces.description: The snapshot it replaced, if it was created to.

status.description:
The worst status among its module's declarations, by the build's
report or, once `verified`, the kernel re-check.

verified.description: Its module and everything it imports have passed the kernel re-check.

version.description: The worker pool version it belongs to.

check.description:
The module's check, as in [`CreateSnapshotResponse::check`], with the
kernel re-check's axioms once it is verified.

exports.description: The declarations that code importing the module sees, in order.

SnapshotDetail.description:
`GET /snapshots/{id}`: a snapshot with its module's code, check and
exports.

SnapshotScope.description:
Which snapshot modules a query searches: `"none"`, `"all"`, or
`{"labels": {"k": "v"}}`, the modules of the snapshots that have every label.

StartSessionRequest.description:
`POST /sessions`: runs code containing `sorry`; each `sorry` becomes a
proof state that tactics can be applied to.

code.description: Code with `sorry`s, each of which becomes a state.

State.description:
A proof state: the goals still to prove. A state stays valid after
tactics are applied to it.

goals.description:
The goals left, as Lean prints them. A session's first states have
their `sorry`'s goal; a tactic can leave more, or none.

id.description: Its id, for applying a tactic at `/states/{id}/tactic`.

pos.description:
Where the `sorry` is in the code. Only a session's first states have
it, not the states that tactics lead to.

TacticInfo.description: One run of a tactic, with the goals before and after it.

goals_after.description:
The goals left after it ran. A tactic that failed, such as an
alternative `first` dropped, leaves them as they were before.

TermInfo.description: A term written in the code, and the type Lean expected it to have.

expr.description: The term as Lean elaborated it.

UpdateSnapshotRequest.description:
`PATCH /snapshots/{id}`: changes the snapshot's labels as a JSON merge
patch, and answers the [`Snapshot`]. The labels that result must follow
the rules of [`check_labels`](crate::labels::check_labels), or nothing
changes.

labels.description:
A label set to `null` is removed, one set to a string takes that
value, and those not named stay as they are.

VerifyFailure.description: A module that failed the kernel re-check.

reason.description: Why the re-check failed, e.g. the kernel's error or a timeout.

VerifySnapshotResponse.description:
`POST /snapshots/{id}/verify`: re-checks the snapshot's module and
everything it imports through the kernel, imports first, skipping what
already passed. A module that fails stops the run and stays usable,
marked as not verified. `verified` and `status` belong to the module, so
every snapshot of it shows the result.

checked.description: The modules this run re-checked and passed, in order.

failure.description: The module that failed, if one did.

snapshot.description: The snapshot, as the re-check left it.

info.description: Checks Lean code, runs proof sessions, keeps snapshots and searches declarations. Errors are `{error: {kind, message}}`, with a status that follows the kind. Search's endpoints are a 404 on a server without search.
info.title: pisa

post.description: Checks code against the version's Lean and imports. The verdict is `ok`; what Lean, the policy or a limit reported is in-band, in `error`, `messages` and `reasons`.

parameters.description:
`respond-async` for a job at once (202), to wait for at
`/jobs/{id}`, rather than the answer.
parameters.name: Prefer

202.description: Queued: wait for its answer at `/jobs/{id}`.

400.description: `bad_request`: the request breaks the API's rules.

404.description:
`not_found`: an unknown or expired job, state, session, snapshot or
declaration.

422.description:
`lean` or `policy`: refused; `timeout`, `out_of_memory` or `crash`: a
limit was hit.

429.description: `capacity`: no worker took the job in time; retry later.

503.description: `unavailable`: e.g. search isn't ready; retry later.

post.description: Each item gets a result, as from `/check`, with its own failure in `error`.

200.description: A result per item, in order

400.description: `bad_request`: the request breaks the API's rules.

404.description:
`not_found`: an unknown or expired job, state, session, snapshot or
declaration.

422.description:
`lean` or `policy`: refused; `timeout`, `out_of_memory` or `crash`: a
limit was hit.

429.description: `capacity`: no worker took the job in time; retry later.

503.description: `unavailable`: e.g. search isn't ready; retry later.

get.description: Its signature, description, flags, dependencies and users: a snapshot's declaration with a snapshot hit's `module`, else the bundle's.

parameters.description: The full name
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: A snapshot module to look in first.
parameters.name: module

parameters.description:
A version, or an alias of one: the index's, or its snapshots'. Any
other is a 404.
parameters.name: version

400.description: `bad_request`: the request breaks the API's rules.

404.description:
`not_found`: an unknown or expired job, state, session, snapshot or
